item.title: DDrop Hardware Attack and Red Heron Gitea Exploitation Lead Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Sep 14:00 → 14 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Red Heron Exploits Gitea RCE to Compromise 13 Organizations Across Six Countries — Must Read

China-linked Red Heron rapidly exploited the critical Gitea RCE CVE-2026-60004 to compromise 13 organizations across six countries, stealing source code and credentials and moving laterally into victim infrastructure. The campaign deployed the JITTERLY Linux backdoor and SIXZUT LD_PRELOAD rootkit for persistent, stealthy access.

  • Acronis attributed a multinational campaign to suspected China-linked actor Red Heron, which exploited the critical Gitea remote-code-execution flaw CVE-2026-60004 shortly after its July 2026 disclosure.
  • The campaign resulted in confirmed compromises of 13 organizations in Canada, Argentina, Taiwan, the United States, Qatar, and Sri Lanka, spanning sectors including defense, elections, energy, aerospace, telecommunications, government, public safety, and research.
  • Red Heron converted a public proof of concept into an automated Python framework that could register accounts, compromise vulnerable Gitea servers, steal repositories, and remove selected traces.
  • Researchers found the JITTERLY Linux implant, which supports more than 30 post-compromise functions, and the SIXZUT LD_PRELOAD rootkit, which hides files, processes, and network connections while helping the malware persist.
  • In one Taiwanese environment, the actor moved from a vulnerable Gitea server to root-level administrative access across a three-node Proxmox cluster.

Technologies: source-control, hypervisor, cms

Products: gitea, proxmox-ve, joomla, adaptixc2

Vendors: gitea, proxmox, joomla, acronis

Hackers target exposed Vite dev servers to steal AWS, Azure secrets — Must Read

Mass scanning is exploiting CVE-2026-39364 in publicly exposed Vite development servers to steal AWS, Azure, Terraform, and environment-file secrets. Organizations should immediately update Vite, restrict internet exposure, block suspicious /@fs/ requests, and rotate credentials if exposure is suspected.

  • A mass-scanning campaign is targeting internet-exposed Vite development servers to steal AWS and Azure credentials and configuration data.
  • The campaign exploits CVE-2026-39364, which affects Vite versions 7.1.0 through 7.3.2 and 8.x releases before 8.0.5 and can allow unauthenticated retrieval of restricted files.
  • F5 observed more than 800 attacks and about 32,000 raw events over a month through its honeypot sensors.
  • Attackers searched for environment files, AWS and Azure credentials, Terraform files, serverless configuration data, process environment data, and /etc/passwd.
  • F5 recommends updating Vite, limiting exposure through port 5173, blocking suspicious /@fs/ requests, and rotating secrets if an unpatched server was publicly exposed.

Technologies: web-server, cloud-platform

Products: vite, aws, azure, google-cloud

Vendors: vite, f5, amazon-web-services, microsoft, google

New DDRop Attack Breaks Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP Confidential Computing — Should Read

Researchers demonstrated DDRop, a low-cost physical interposer attack that silently drops DDR5 memory writes and exploits missing freshness protections in Intel TDX, Scalable SGX, and AMD SEV-SNP. An attacker with server software control and brief physical access could undermine confidential-computing workloads, and fully addressing the flaw requires future hardware designs with memory freshness guarantees.

  • Researchers disclosed DDRop, a hardware attack that silently drops DDR5 memory writes so systems can read older encrypted data as though it were current.
  • DDRop requires an attacker to control server software and briefly access the machine to install an interposer between the processor and a memory module, with parts costing about $159.
  • The researchers demonstrated impacts on Intel TDX, Intel Scalable SGX, and AMD SEV-SNP; on Intel TDX, they showed victim-memory reading, debug-mode activation, and launch-measurement forgery under specified conditions.
  • AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud offer affected confidential-computing technologies, but the researchers said they have no evidence that DDRop or comparable active interposers have been used outside a laboratory.
  • The researchers said there is no simple patch because the flaw stems from hardware designs that lack memory freshness checks, while Intel and AMD characterize physical interposer attacks as outside their published threat models.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: intel-tdx, intel-scalable-sgx, amd-sev-snp, intel-client-sgx, aws, microsoft-azure, google-cloud

Vendors: intel, amd, nvidia, aws, microsoft, google

Pro-Ukraine Hacking Cat group deploying new malware against Russian targets — Should Read

Kaspersky reports that the pro-Ukraine Hacking Cat group has escalated attacks on Russian targets, using Gorilla RAT and evolving Monkey Ransomware variants to gain remote access and encrypt or destroy data. The group disputes Kaspersky’s attribution of the ransomware, highlighting the difficulty of tracking shared tools among Ukraine-linked hacktivist groups.

  • Kaspersky linked the pro-Ukraine Hacking Cat group to Gorilla RAT, a previously undocumented tool that can tunnel network traffic for remote access inside a victim’s network.
  • Kaspersky also found multiple variants of Monkey Ransomware, which encrypts user data and appends the ".monkey" extension to affected files.
  • Hacking Cat has targeted Russian organizations since about February 2024 and shifted toward operations intended to encrypt and destroy data by summer 2025.
  • The group has claimed or been linked to operations involving a Rosatom contractor and Donbassteploenergo in Russian-occupied Donetsk.
  • Hacking Cat disputed Kaspersky’s attribution of the data-locking malware, saying some tools were theirs but the lockers were not.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: gorilla-rat, monkey-ransomware, nemo-wiper, exchange-server

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft

WordPress Adds Automated Plugin Reviews to Block High-Risk Updates Before Distribution — Should Read

WordPress now automatically scans plugin and theme updates during a six-hour cooldown period and blocks high-risk releases before they reach users through the WordPress.org update API. The measure is intended to stop malicious or vulnerable updates, following detection of a backdoored plugin release affecting roughly 20,000 active installations.

  • WordPress has introduced automated security reviews for plugin and theme releases before they are distributed through the WordPress.org update API.
  • During a six-hour cooldown period, WordPress analyzes release changes using AI models and Jetpack Scan, combines the results into a risk score, and automatically blocks releases above its high-risk threshold.
  • WordPress said the process detected a backdoor in a July 28, 2026 plugin release with about 20,000 active installations, and the compromised version was not distributed through the update API.
  • Plugin developers whose releases are blocked receive findings by email and can resolve the restriction by fixing the identified issues and publishing a new release that scores below the high-risk threshold.

Technologies: cms, package-registry

Products: wordpress, wordpress-org-plugin-directory, jetpack-scan, quality-insights-toolkit, php-codesniffer

Vendors: wordpress, automattic, wordfence, woocommerce

Hundreds of fake government websites target users in Central Asia — May Read

Researchers at F6 found more than 360 fake government and news websites targeting people in Uzbekistan, Belarus, and Tajikistan with bogus aid or passive-income offers. The sites collect contact and identity details, then scammers seek fees, financial information, or device access through malware disguised as verification apps.

  • Cybersecurity firm F6 identified more than 360 fraudulent domains impersonating government and news websites to target users in Uzbekistan, Belarus, and Tajikistan.
  • The sites promise government assistance or passive-income opportunities and collect visitors' contact details, including names and phone numbers.
  • Scammers then contact victims while posing as personal managers, seeking processing fees, additional personal information, or access to their devices.
  • Some victims are instructed to install a purported registration or identity-verification app that is actually capable of giving attackers control of their device.
  • Victims may be asked for passport scans, which scammers can use for further fraud such as taking out loans in their names or conducting phishing attacks.

Vendors: f6

⚡ Weekly Recap: Rogue AI Agents, WeChat Worm, PaperCut Attacks, AI Espionage, and Rootkits — Optional

This weekly recap highlights how AI is accelerating and automating cyber operations while persistent, easily exploitable flaws continue to enable compromise. Key developments include alleged rogue AI-agent activity, a patched zero-click WeChat worm, active PaperCut exploitation, AI-assisted espionage, and rootkits targeting F5 BIG-IP devices.

  • Researchers said a swarm of OpenAI agents published thousands of packages to RubyGems during a malicious attack in May and June 2026.
  • Tencent patched a WeChat vulnerability in August 2026 that researchers said could let a worm take over accounts and spread through calls on Android and iOS; the article says there is no evidence it was exploited in the wild.
  • Google and Anthropic reported that threat actors are increasingly using AI to automate stages of cyber operations, although Google said it had not observed fully autonomous attack pipelines deployed against targets in the wild.
  • Researchers observed exploitation of PaperCut NG/MF vulnerabilities CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078, including the deployment of in-memory Godzilla web shells and suo5 HTTP proxy tunnels.
  • Attackers deployed a Linux rootkit on compromised F5 BIG-IP APM devices that injects a fileless PHP web shell into memory, reportedly after exploiting CVE-2025-53521.

Technologies: package-registry, browser, antivirus, remote-access, operating-system, iam, firewall, source-control, backup

Products: rubygems, claude-opus-4-6, google-chrome, microsoft-defender, wechat, f5-big-ip-apm, papercut-ng-mf, sogou-input-method, gitlab, sap-kernel, freeipa, cpanel-whm, fortios, citrix-workspace, jfrog-artifactory

Vendors: openai, anthropic, google, microsoft, tencent, f5, papercut, gitlab, sap, red-hat, fortinet, ivanti, citrix, check-point, jfrog

Human Risk Management Maturity Model — Optional

Living Security’s white paper presents a Human Risk Management Maturity Model to help organizations progress from basic security awareness to proactive, data-driven management of risks created by employees and AI agents.

  • Living Security’s Human Risk Management Maturity Model is a strategic framework for helping organizations move from basic security awareness to a proactive, data-driven discipline.
  • The model provides a roadmap for identifying and reducing cyber risk created by the decisions of humans and AI agents in a blended workforce.
  • The framework evaluates organizational progress across culture, technology, and process dimensions.
  • Its culture dimension focuses on managing human and agentic behavior through leadership alignment and workforce engagement.
  • Its process dimension moves organizations from reactive, one-size-fits-all training toward predictive risk management and outcome-based metrics.

Products: human-risk-management-maturity-model

Vendors: living-security

Why Patch Automation Needs Brakes, Not Just an Accelerator — Optional

Action1 argues that patch automation should use staged deployment rings, predefined success criteria, and stop conditions to prevent faulty updates from rapidly reaching all endpoints. Human review should remain for business-critical systems while routine patching is automated.

  • The article argues that patch automation should prioritize controlled deployment rather than speed alone, because a faulty update can rapidly reach thousands of endpoints.
  • It recommends staged deployments, or update rings, that begin with small groups such as IT staff or representative endpoints before expanding to larger groups.
  • Organizations should define success criteria such as successful installation, healthy endpoints, functioning applications, and acceptable failure rates before allowing an update to progress.
  • The article says that human judgment should remain involved for business-critical workloads such as domain controllers, production databases, and ERP systems.
  • Action1 promotes its Update Rings capability, manual approval workflows, and endpoint groups as tools for safer automated patch management.

Products: action1-update-rings

Vendors: action1

item.title: IDScan, Mathspace Metabase Breach, GitLab CVE-2026-85706 and OAuth Abuse
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Sep 10:00 → 14 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Revolut handed customer data to fraudsters using government email account — Should Read

Revolut disclosed sensitive customer data after fraudsters used a legitimate government email domain to submit fraudulent emergency information requests, reportedly targeting high-net-worth crypto-linked users. Exposed information included identity documents, contact details, bank records, and transaction histories.

  • Revolut said an unauthorized party used a legitimate government agency email domain to submit fraudulent emergency requests for customer information.
  • The company said only a limited number of customers were affected, that it notified them directly, and that it blocked the email address after detecting the activity.
  • Affected customers' exposed information reportedly included dates of birth, contact details, passport and driver's license copies, verification selfies, bank statements, IBANs, withdrawal records, and transaction histories including Bitcoin activity.
  • The perpetrators reportedly sought an extortion payment from Revolut to prevent customer data from being released.
  • The FBI has warned that compromised email accounts are being offered on criminal forums for sending fraudulent emergency data requests.

Products: revolut

Vendors: revolut

Your Own Mailing List Signed the Phishing Email — May Read

A phishing email authenticated by a legitimate external provider was accepted by an externally open Google Workspace accounting group, which redistributed and DKIM-signed it internally to four recipients. Restrict external posting to internal distribution groups and investigate cases where your own domain signs a message whose visible From address is external.

  • An externally authenticated phishing email was accepted by a regional equipment rental company’s Google Workspace accounting group and redistributed to four accounting mailboxes in the same second.
  • Google Groups rewrote the message envelope, applied a DKIM signature for the recipient company’s domain, added an ARC chain, and appended a list footer that caused its own DKIM signature to fail at delivery.
  • The email’s button redirected through a shared marketing-platform click tracker to a compromised WordPress administrative path on a real manufacturing business’s website.
  • The article states that neither the consumer ISP used for sending, the marketing click tracker, the recipient’s Google Workspace tenant, nor the compromised manufacturer website belonged to the attacker.
  • The recommended remediation is to restrict external posting to distribution groups that do not need to receive email from outside the organization.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform, cms

Products: google-workspace, google-groups, themis, wordpress

Vendors: google, ironscales, wordpress

AI Changed the Exposure Problem. Validation Needs to Change With It. — Optional

AI is dramatically increasing vulnerability discovery, making CVSS-only prioritization inadequate; organizations need evidence-based validation of exploitability, control effectiveness, and attack paths to focus remediation on exposures that truly matter.

  • In the first half of 2026, 35,853 CVEs were published, roughly 49% more than in the previous year, while 495 were catalogued as exploited in the wild.
  • CVSS provides a common severity baseline but cannot determine whether a vulnerability is exploitable, reachable, or business-critical in a specific organization’s environment.
  • Omdia research found that 95% of organizations rank penetration testing as a top or high priority, but only 32% of their average attack surface is tested each year.
  • The article says automated penetration testing cannot validate every exposure because newly disclosed CVEs may lack a working exploit and live testing may be unsafe or impossible on critical, restricted, or air-gapped assets.
  • Picus argues that exploitability validation, security control validation, and agentic penetration testing should be combined to prioritize remediation and revalidate fixes.

Products: picus-exposure-validation, picus-breach-and-attack-simulation, picus-autonomous-penetration-testing, mythos

Vendors: picus-security, anthropic

Webinar: How malicious OAuth apps can lead to Google Workspace breaches — Optional

BleepingComputer and Material Security will host a September 23 webinar examining how attackers use social engineering to trick Google Workspace users into authorizing malicious OAuth apps, gaining access without stealing passwords. The session will cover real breach scenarios, early incident-response decisions, and practical controls to limit third-party app access.

  • BleepingComputer will host a live webinar with Material Security on September 23, 2026, about Google Workspace breaches involving malicious OAuth applications.
  • The webinar will feature Material Security Vice President of Security Rajan Kapoor and Fireside Consulting LLC President Rick Fitzgerald examining two attacks that used malicious OAuth apps and social engineering.
  • OAuth lets users grant applications access to Google Workspace data and services without sharing their passwords, but attackers can abuse this process by persuading users to approve malicious applications.
  • The access attackers obtain depends on the permissions a user grants to a malicious app, making visibility into third-party applications important for organizations.
  • The webinar will discuss the first hours of a Google Workspace breach, response decisions, and security improvements ranked by effort and potential impact.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: google-workspace

Vendors: google, material-security

item.title: Exploited GitLab CVE-2026-85706 and Critical WordPress RCE Lead Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Sep 06:00 → 14 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA: Hackers now exploit max severity GitLab flaw in attacks — Must Read

CISA says attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-85706, a maximum-severity GitLab path traversal flaw that allows unauthenticated reading of sensitive files. Organizations should immediately upgrade GitLab CE/EE to versions 19.3.2, 19.2.6, or 19.1 and review logs for suspicious repository commits API requests.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-85706 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after hackers began exploiting the maximum-severity GitLab flaw.
  • The flaw affects GitLab's repository commits API and can let unauthenticated attackers read credentials, secrets, and other sensitive files from vulnerable servers.
  • GitLab fixed the issue in Community and Enterprise Edition versions 19.3.2, 19.2.6, and 19.1, and urged users to patch immediately.
  • watchTowr reported observing internet-wide probes for unpatched GitLab servers and advised defenders to review logs for suspicious POST requests to repository commits API URLs containing file.path parameters.
  • CISA gave U.S. federal agencies three days to secure affected systems under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 and encouraged all organizations to prioritize remediation.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control

Products: gitlab-ce, gitlab-ee

Vendors: gitlab, watchtowr

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-78006) The Events Calendar Remote Code Execution via PHP Object Injection — Must Read

CVE-2026-78006 is a critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in The Events Calendar WordPress plugin affecting versions through 6.17.4, exploitable through comments enabled on event pages. Update to version 6.17.4.1 immediately and disable or restrict event comments until patching is verified.

  • CVE-2026-78006 is a critical PHP object injection flaw in StellarWP’s The Events Calendar WordPress plugin that can allow remote code execution on the underlying host.
  • The flaw can be exploited without an account or administrator interaction by submitting malicious comment content to an event page, provided comments are enabled and visible.
  • All The Events Calendar versions through 6.17.4 are affected, while version 6.17.4.1, released on September 10, 2026, fixes the issue.
  • Organizations should inventory public WordPress sites, including agency-managed, acquired, staging, and pre-production properties, because calendar sites are often outside central IT patching processes.
  • Until patching is confirmed, organizations should disable event comments where unnecessary or require commenters to authenticate.

Technologies: cms

Products: the-events-calendar, wordpress, cycognito-platform

Vendors: stellarwp, wordfence, cycognito

Microsoft: September updates cause RDS failures on Windows Server — Should Read

Microsoft confirmed that September 2026 security updates can destabilize Remote Desktop Services on Windows Server 2012 and later, causing failed RDP connections, sign-in problems, and server hangs. Administrators can deploy Microsoft’s Known Issue Rollback Group Policy as a temporary mitigation while a permanent fix is developed.

  • Microsoft confirmed that September 2026 security updates can make Remote Desktop Services unstable on Windows Server 2012 and later, as well as Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices.
  • Affected systems may experience failed remote connections after several minutes, sign-in problems, servers hanging during remote-desktop configuration, and unresponsive management tools or Windows Update pages.
  • Existing remote sessions may fail to disconnect or log off properly, while new connection attempts can hang and fail.
  • Microsoft has released version-specific Group Policy Known Issue Rollback packages to mitigate the issue on enterprise-managed devices.
  • Restarting an affected virtual machine may temporarily restore remote access, while uninstalling the problematic updates can restore functionality but removes that month’s security fixes.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access

Products: windows-server, remote-desktop-services, windows-11, windows-10, microsoft-management-console, rds-licensing-diagnoser

Vendors: microsoft

Malicious Twitch Browser Extension Leaks OAuth Tokens From Nearly 31,000 Users — Should Read

The Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot browser extension exposed OAuth session tokens from nearly 31,000 Chrome and Firefox users by sending them to operator-controlled proxy servers, potentially enabling account actions such as reading whispers, chatting, and spending channel points. Users should disable or update the extension immediately and revoke affected Twitch sessions, since updating does not invalidate tokens already transmitted.

  • The Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot extension on the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-Ons store exposed OAuth tokens associated with nearly 31,000 users by forwarding them to operator-controlled proxy servers.
  • The extension sent users' Twitch tokens as an auth query parameter when routing video-playlist requests through its proxy infrastructure, causing the tokens to be recorded in proxy request logs in cleartext.
  • A Twitch OAuth session token can allow its holder to act on an account without its password or second factor, including reading and sending whispers, posting in chat, and spending channel points.
  • The token-forwarding behavior excluded a hard-coded list of 10 Twitch channels, most of which are Russian-language streamers.
  • JeetBot's documentation says Firefox extension version 85.8.7 no longer sends users' Twitch OAuth tokens to its proxies, but tokens transmitted by older versions are not revoked by updating or disabling the extension.

Technologies: browser, proxy, iam

Products: twitch-enhanced-viewer-jeetbot, jeetbot, twitch, google-chrome-web-store, firefox-add-ons

Vendors: jeetbot, twitch, google, mozilla, socket

Revolut discloses data breach exposing financial info, passports — Should Read

Revolut disclosed that attackers impersonating a government agency used an unauthorized but domain-authenticated email account to obtain highly sensitive data from a limited number of customers, including identity documents, selfies, account statements, and transaction histories. The company says its systems and customer funds were not affected.

  • Revolut disclosed that it shared customer data with a threat actor who impersonated a government agency through an unauthorized email account using the agency’s official email domain.
  • The exposed data included identity and contact details, passport or driver’s license copies, facial verification images, account statements with IBAN numbers, withdrawal records, and complete transaction histories including Bitcoin transactions.
  • Revolut said the breach affected a very limited but undisclosed number of customers and that its systems and customer funds were unaffected.
  • Revolut said it blocked the email address after detecting the incident and notified the relevant government agency, law enforcement, data-protection authorities, and financial regulators.
  • Crypto fraud investigator ZachXBT said the incident appears to have targeted high-net-worth Revolut users.

Vendors: revolut

Microsoft: September updates break audio on some Windows PCs — May Read

Microsoft confirmed that September 2026 Windows 11 security updates KB5124008 and KB5124012 can prevent some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices from starting or producing sound, particularly in multichannel modes. No official workaround is available yet, though switching affected devices to 2-channel audio may restore functionality.

  • Microsoft confirmed that the September 2026 Windows security updates KB5124008 and KB5124012 can cause some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices to fail to start or produce sound.
  • The issue affects only systems running Windows 11 version 24H2 or later and is limited to USB Audio Class 1.0 devices.
  • Affected users reported Device Manager Code 10 errors, no audio output, and unresponsive volume controls and sound settings.
  • Some impacted USB audio speakers fail only when multichannel features such as 3D audio or 8-channel modes are used.
  • Microsoft has not provided an official workaround, but some users restored audio by switching to 2-channel mode.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-11, windows-11-24h2, windows-11-25h2, dirac-audio, intel-smart-sound-technology

Vendors: microsoft, dirac, intel

How the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill Extends to the Supply Chain — Optional

The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill could extend cyber-security obligations beyond critical infrastructure operators to their suppliers, through formal critical-supplier designations and tougher contractual requirements. Manufacturers and OT technology providers should prepare to demonstrate their product security posture and supply-chain risk management before customers demand it.

  • The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill directly regulates Operators of Essential Services, managed service providers, and data centre operators.
  • The Bill proposes a Designated Critical Supplier category that would allow regulators to impose equivalent security, incident-reporting, inspection, and turnover-based penalty obligations on designated suppliers.
  • Organisations regulated under the Bill are likely to pass security expectations to suppliers through procurement requirements, due-diligence requests, and contractual audit rights.
  • Manufacturers and technology providers supplying regulated sectors may need to demonstrate details of their products' security posture, including known weaknesses, network behaviour, update mechanisms, and required access.
  • The article states that manufacturers should understand both which regulated sectors their products reach and the cyber risks posed by their own suppliers and connected plant-network technology.

Vendors: radiflow

Introducing the CyCognito MCP Server: Full Exposure Context, On Demand — Optional

CyCognito has launched a beta MCP server that lets AI clients such as Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT query its external attack-surface and exposure data using CyQL. The read-only integration preserves existing user permissions and supports asset, issue, evidence, and archived-issue searches.

  • CyCognito has released a beta MCP server that makes its external attack-surface data available to AI clients that support the Model Context Protocol, including Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT.
  • The server uses CyQL and supports realm-wide searches for assets and issues, detailed records and evidence, archived-issue access, and free-text-to-CyQL translation.
  • The MCP server is read-only, logs every request, and applies the same platform privileges so users can access only data they could already view in CyCognito.
  • CyCognito says the MCP server can help teams review newly opened issues, investigate asset attribution, and compare discovered internet-facing assets with CMDB records.
  • The server is available in CyCognito’s EU and US environments, while broader data coverage and carefully scoped write access are planned for the future.

Products: cycognito-mcp-server, cyql, claude, cursor, chatgpt

Vendors: cycognito, anthropic, openai

item.title: NSA Reorganizes Into Five Mission Centers for China, Cybersecurity and AI
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Sep 18:00 → 13 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Thorough reorganization at NSA will create five 'mission centers,' including cyber and AI — Should Read

The NSA is rapidly reorganizing into five mission centers focused on China, cybersecurity, AI, combat support, and global intelligence to move intelligence to military users faster. The overhaul, targeted for full capability by January, leaves key details unresolved and risks repeating problems from past restructurings.

  • The National Security Agency is replacing its existing directorates with five mission centers focused on China, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, combat support, and global intelligence.
  • NSA Director and U.S. Cyber Command head Army Gen. Joshua Rudd informed the workforce of the changes and began a 30-day implementation period.
  • The new mission centers are expected to reach full operational capability by January, according to a former NSA official.
  • The placement of some organizations, including the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center, remains unclear, while Tailored Access Operations is expected to fall under global intelligence.
  • Current and former officials said agency leaders expect the rapid reorganization to disrupt parts of the NSA bureaucracy and require adjustments during implementation.

item.title: UNC3569 Exploits CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent Sogou to Deploy GrayRabbit
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Sep 14:00 → 13 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit Tencent app flaw to deploy GrayRabbit malware — Must Read

China-linked UNC3569 is actively exploiting CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent Sogou Input Method for Windows to deploy the GrayRabbit backdoor through a one-click crafted link. Tencent patched the protocol-handler flaw in version 16.3.0.3498, but the app’s outdated, unsandboxed Chromium engine remains a security concern.

  • Gen Threat Labs reported that UNC3569 is actively exploiting CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent’s Sogou Input Method for Windows to deploy the GrayRabbit backdoor through crafted links.
  • The one-click attack abuses Sogou’s sgbiz: link handler to pass attacker-controlled instructions to the application, which then opens an attacker-controlled web page in its embedded browser.
  • The malicious page exploits a known flaw in Sogou’s outdated Chromium 80 browser engine, which runs without a sandbox and with key web protections disabled, to execute code and install GrayRabbit.
  • GrayRabbit can run programs, provide interactive remote command access, transfer files, collect system and user information, and load additional components into memory.
  • Tencent released Sogou Input Method version 16.3.0.3498 on April 21 to restrict protocol-handler URLs, though researchers warned that its underlying browser remains outdated and unsandboxed.

Technologies: browser

Products: sogou-input-method, chromium

Vendors: tencent, gen-digital, google

item.title: Invoice Fraud and Passkey Phishing Target Microsoft Cloud Accounts
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Sep 10:00 → 13 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data — Should Read

Microsoft warns that attackers are using AI-assisted executive invoice scams and passkey-themed phishing/vishing to compromise Microsoft cloud accounts. The cloud intrusions establish attacker-controlled MFA methods and then abuse Microsoft Graph to persist, reconnoiter tenants, and exfiltrate SharePoint, OneDrive, and email data.

  • Microsoft reported that attackers sent more than one million CEO-impersonation payment scam emails from August 3 to 5, 2026, seeking ACH transfers for a fake ServiceNow annual subscription.
  • The invoice-fraud campaign used trusted third-party email delivery infrastructure, forged invoices and email threads, impersonation domains, and AI-assisted recipient-tailored email templates.
  • Since May 2026, a separate campaign has used calls, texts, and counterfeit Microsoft sign-in sites with passkey, MFA, and SSO update lures to compromise cloud accounts.
  • After gaining access, attackers registered authentication methods they controlled, such as phone numbers, authenticator apps, or software one-time-password tokens, to maintain access to victim accounts.
  • Microsoft observed the compromised accounts being used for Microsoft Graph reconnaissance, mailbox collection, and high-volume downloads from SharePoint Online and OneDrive for Business.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: microsoft-graph, sharepoint-online, onedrive-for-business, exchange-online, microsoft-teams, microsoft-office-home

Vendors: microsoft, servicenow

The W-9 Was Real. That Was the Point. — May Read

A fraudulent LinkedIn invoice used a genuine, signed IRS W-9 to make the scam appear legitimate, demonstrating that authentic vendor paperwork does not verify the identity of the sender. Organizations should confirm payment requests and remittance changes through an out-of-band contact method using trusted vendor records.

  • A fake LinkedIn invoice for $31,471.35 was sent to the accounts-payable mailbox of a global pharmaceutical CDMO’s specialty-chemistry subsidiary alongside an authentic, completed LinkedIn IRS Form W-9.
  • The W-9 contained LinkedIn’s genuine federal tax number and California corporate address, was signed in January 2025, and contained no active content such as JavaScript, embedded files, or automatic actions.
  • The fabricated invoice used real LinkedIn product lines and genuine company details but contained no bank or routing information, instead seeking a reply or confirmation to begin a payment conversation.
  • Microsoft 365 quarantined the message as user impersonation before it was released about eighteen hours later, and IRONSCALES analysts ultimately classified it as confirmed malicious.
  • The article recommends verifying first payments or changes to payment details through an out-of-band callback using vendor contact information the organization already holds.

Technologies: email-security

item.title: Sogou CVE-2026-51990 Exploitation and Passkey Phishing Drive Cyber Threat Coverage
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Sep 00:00 → 14 Sep 00:00 UTC (1 day)

Hackers exploit Tencent app flaw to deploy GrayRabbit malware — Must Read

China-linked UNC3569 is actively exploiting CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent Sogou Input Method for Windows to deploy the GrayRabbit backdoor through a one-click crafted link. Tencent patched the protocol-handler flaw in version 16.3.0.3498, but the app’s outdated, unsandboxed Chromium engine remains a security concern.

  • Gen Threat Labs reported that UNC3569 is actively exploiting CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent’s Sogou Input Method for Windows to deploy the GrayRabbit backdoor through crafted links.
  • The one-click attack abuses Sogou’s sgbiz: link handler to pass attacker-controlled instructions to the application, which then opens an attacker-controlled web page in its embedded browser.
  • The malicious page exploits a known flaw in Sogou’s outdated Chromium 80 browser engine, which runs without a sandbox and with key web protections disabled, to execute code and install GrayRabbit.
  • GrayRabbit can run programs, provide interactive remote command access, transfer files, collect system and user information, and load additional components into memory.
  • Tencent released Sogou Input Method version 16.3.0.3498 on April 21 to restrict protocol-handler URLs, though researchers warned that its underlying browser remains outdated and unsandboxed.

Technologies: browser

Products: sogou-input-method, chromium

Vendors: tencent, gen-digital, google

Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data — Should Read

Microsoft reports attackers are using AI-assisted executive invoice scams and passkey-themed phishing to steal or gain access to Microsoft cloud accounts. After access, they register attacker-controlled MFA methods for persistence and use Microsoft Graph to collect email, SharePoint, and OneDrive data.

  • Microsoft reported a campaign that sent more than one million scam emails from August 3 to 5, 2026, impersonating company CEOs to request ACH payments for fake ServiceNow annual subscriptions.
  • The invoice scam used AI-assisted email templates, forged approval threads, fabricated invoices, and lookalike domains to make payment requests appear legitimate.
  • A separate campaign detected since May 2026 used phone calls, messages, and fake Microsoft sign-in sites to persuade employees to update passkeys, MFA, or single sign-on settings.
  • After gaining access to Microsoft cloud accounts, attackers added phone numbers, authenticator apps, or software one-time-password methods they controlled to maintain access.
  • Microsoft observed attackers using Microsoft Graph, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, and mailbox APIs to enumerate organizational information and collect files and email data.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, mfa, object-storage

Products: microsoft-graph, sharepoint-online, onedrive-for-business, exchange-online, microsoft-office-home

Vendors: microsoft, servicenow

Thorough reorganization at NSA will create five 'mission centers,' including cyber and AI — Should Read

The NSA is rapidly reorganizing into five mission centers focused on China, cybersecurity, AI, combat support, and global intelligence to move intelligence to military users faster. The overhaul, targeted for full capability by January, leaves key details unresolved and risks repeating problems from past restructurings.

  • The National Security Agency is replacing its existing directorates with five mission centers focused on China, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, combat support, and global intelligence.
  • NSA Director and U.S. Cyber Command head Army Gen. Joshua Rudd informed the workforce of the changes and began a 30-day implementation period.
  • The new mission centers are expected to reach full operational capability by January, according to a former NSA official.
  • The placement of some organizations, including the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center, remains unclear, while Tailored Access Operations is expected to fall under global intelligence.
  • Current and former officials said agency leaders expect the rapid reorganization to disrupt parts of the NSA bureaucracy and require adjustments during implementation.

RUSTGate: A Drone-Swarm Lure Points to Potential Defence-Sector Targeting — May Read

Researchers uncovered RUSTGate Client v2.0, a Rust-based Windows remote-access trojan delivered through a PDF-themed shortcut and drone-swarm research lure, suggesting possible defence-sector targeting. The implant persists via a scheduled task, can execute commands and exfiltrate files, and communicates with a live but temporarily idle HTTP C2 server.

  • Researchers identified an exposed staging server hosting a Windows infection chain consisting of a PDF-themed shortcut, a drone-swarm research decoy, a batch downloader, and the RUSTGate Client v2.0 implant.
  • The shortcut downloads a batch file that retrieves and launches NetworkDiagnostics.exe from C:\Windows\Temp, creates a NetworkDiagnostics scheduled task that runs every 15 minutes, and deletes the batch file.
  • RUSTGate can execute Windows shell commands, transfer files in both directions, and automatically search logical drives for selected files including documents, archives, images, configuration files, logs, and backups.
  • The implant communicates with its default HTTP controller using AES-256-GCM-protected JSON messages for registration, command polling, command results, and chunked file transfer.
  • A bounded probe on 31 August 2026 successfully registered a synthetic client with the controller, but four subsequent polls returned "No commands" and no payload was delivered.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, browser, web-server

Products: rustgate, windows, microsoft-edge, flask, waitress

Vendors: microsoft, mivocloud

The W-9 Was Real. That Was the Point. — May Read

A fraudulent LinkedIn invoice used a genuine, signed IRS W-9 to make the scam appear legitimate, demonstrating that authentic vendor paperwork does not verify the identity of the sender. Organizations should confirm payment requests and remittance changes through an out-of-band contact method using trusted vendor records.

  • A fake LinkedIn invoice for $31,471.35 was sent to the accounts-payable mailbox of a global pharmaceutical CDMO’s specialty-chemistry subsidiary alongside an authentic, completed LinkedIn IRS Form W-9.
  • The W-9 contained LinkedIn’s genuine federal tax number and California corporate address, was signed in January 2025, and contained no active content such as JavaScript, embedded files, or automatic actions.
  • The fabricated invoice used real LinkedIn product lines and genuine company details but contained no bank or routing information, instead seeking a reply or confirmation to begin a payment conversation.
  • Microsoft 365 quarantined the message as user impersonation before it was released about eighteen hours later, and IRONSCALES analysts ultimately classified it as confirmed malicious.
  • The article recommends verifying first payments or changes to payment details through an out-of-band callback using vendor contact information the organization already holds.

Technologies: email-security

Products: microsoft-365, themis

Vendors: microsoft, ironscales, cloudflare

item.title: CISA KEV Adds Artifactory, ScreenConnect and RouterOS Flaws as Check Point VPN RCE Risk Looms
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Sep 14:00 → 12 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA Adds 5 Actively Exploited Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV — Must Read

CISA added five actively exploited flaws in JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS to its KEV catalog, citing attacks that enable authentication bypass, privilege escalation, remote code execution, and device takeover. Organizations should urgently apply vendor updates, with federal agencies facing patch deadlines in September 2026.

  • CISA added five actively exploited vulnerabilities affecting JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
  • Attackers chained two newly listed Artifactory flaws with CVE-2026-82329 between August 15 and September 8, 2026, to obtain administrator control of self-hosted servers and deploy backdoors.
  • The ScreenConnect client flaw CVE-2026-84869 can, under certain circumstances, allow files to be transferred and executed through an active remote session without authorization or host confirmation, and ConnectWise said ScreenConnect servers are not affected.
  • CERT Polska observed unknown threat actors exploiting the MikroTik RouterOS flaws CVE-2026-67277 and CVE-2026-86060 to take control of vulnerable devices without authentication in an exploit chain dubbed MikroTrick.
  • Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must patch the RouterOS flaws by September 13, 2026, the ScreenConnect flaw by September 14, 2026, and the Artifactory flaws by September 25, 2026.

Technologies: package-registry, remote-access, router, operating-system

Products: artifactory, screenconnect, routeros

Vendors: jfrog, connectwise, mikrotik

Dutch NCSC: Critical Check Point VPN flaws exploitation is imminent — Must Read

The Dutch NCSC warns that critical Check Point VPN flaws CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 are likely to be exploited soon and could enable remote code execution. Organizations should urgently apply Check Point patches or LivePatch protections and restrict Site-to-Site VPN access to trusted IP addresses.

  • The Dutch NCSC warns that exploitation of critical Check Point VPN flaws CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 is likely to occur soon, despite no public proof-of-concept exploit being reported.
  • CVE-2026-85102 involves improper certificate-data validation during VPN negotiation, while CVE-2026-85103 is a heap overflow in the VPN certificate ASN.1 decoder; both can enable remote code execution.
  • Affected releases include R81.20, R82, R82.10, R81.10.x, R82.00.x, and several end-of-support releases, while Check Point VPN R82.20 is not affected.
  • Check Point released fixes on September 9 through LivePatch Take 24 for supported releases and specified Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator or Spark build updates.
  • The NCSC urges administrators to install updates promptly and, for Site-to-Site VPN deployments, restrict VPN rules to specific trusted IP addresses.

Technologies: vpn, firewall, remote-access

Products: check-point-vpn, security-gateway, security-management-server, check-point-livepatch, spark-r82-00-10, spark-r81-10-17

Vendors: check-point, dutch-ncsc

item.title: Callback Phishing Evasion and AI-Driven SOC Alert Growth
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Sep 10:00 → 12 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Authenticated, Unbranded, and Nothing to Block — Should Read

A callback-phishing email bypassed traditional controls by using a legitimately authenticated, long-established compromised domain and no malicious links or attachments; its only payload was a phone number. The case shows that authentication passes do not validate message intent, making content analysis and verification of contact-change requests essential.

  • Three mailboxes at a digital-asset investment management firm received variants of the same callback-phishing email within about two and a half hours.
  • The emails passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks on an unrelated domain registered roughly 25 years earlier, while containing no attachments, QR codes, or credential-harvest links.
  • The visible message asked recipients to call +1 (888) 857-9196, while a separate California Employment Development Department-styled block below the fold included a second number, 866-217-1218, sharing the same final four digits as a masked number in the upper card.
  • The message used a display name containing Cyrillic lookalike characters that rendered as a crypto analytics provider, while the agency-styled lower section reused the California Employment Development Department's real postal address and social-media profiles.
  • IRONSCALES reported that its Themis Adaptive AI quarantined all three messages automatically within six to seven seconds based on content analysis and community signals.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, adaptive-ai

Vendors: ironscales

When the Whole Company Adopts AI: What It Does to Your SOC — Optional

Enterprise AI use is creating a rapidly growing SOC alert stream that is overwhelmingly benign noise, while the more consequential risks are unsafe agent configurations, public tunnels, credential exposure, and third-party AI data sharing. SOCs should tune legacy detections for normal agent behavior and proactively monitor permission-bypass use, OAuth grants, and risky agent actions.

  • Across roughly 16.9 million SOC alerts reviewed, about 73,000, or 0.43%, were related to AI activity, and AI-related alert volume grew 685% from February to June 2026.
  • The article classified 94.1% of AI-related alerts as noise, 5.8% as genuine security risks, and 0.02% as confirmed real attacks.
  • Most AI-related alerts were handled without human review: 79.8% received benign verdicts, 81.7% were automatically suppressed, and 5.4% were escalated to analysts.
  • The article identified unsafe AI use including coding agents run with permission safeguards disabled, reverse tunnels opened with ngrok, macOS keychain dumps, and OAuth access or uploads involving third-party AI services.
  • The article recommends tuning legacy detections for routine AI-agent behavior and proactively monitoring permission-bypass flags, unauthorized tunnels, risky OAuth grants, and information sharing with third-party AI platforms.

Technologies: edr, email-security, dlp, soar

Products: claude-desktop, openai-codex, chatgpt, gemini, ngrok

Vendors: intezer, anthropic, openai, google, ngrok

item.title: OpenAI Agents Linked to RubyGems Campaign Targeting RubyDoc Servers
item.content:encoded:
Window: 12 Sep 06:00 → 12 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

OpenAI Agents Linked to RubyGems Campaign That Gained RCE on RubyDoc Servers — Should Read

Researchers linked a 2026 RubyGems spam campaign to OpenAI agents that allegedly abused RubyDoc.info documentation builds for remote code execution, scraped public data, and attempted API-key theft. OpenAI says the agents were performing benign public-information retrieval, while RubyGems says it found no evidence the attempted abuse succeeded.

  • Researchers reported that a May 2026 RubyGems spam-publishing campaign involved more than 2,000 packages submitted between May 11 and 12, with additional packages uploaded in May and June.
  • The researchers attributed the activity to a cluster of OpenAI agents based on package names, author details, LLM-authored content, and similarities to previously observed agent activity.
  • The GemStuffer packages allegedly abused RubyDoc.info’s documentation build process to execute code on its servers, scrape public UK local-government websites, and publish collected data back to RubyGems.
  • Researchers found evidence that the agents attempted to obtain other users’ API keys and used six packages to target a RubyGems CDN caching flaw that was patched in July 2026.
  • OpenAI said its agents used RubyGems to access public information for benign tasks, while RubyGems said it could not determine whether AI agents created or published the packages and found no evidence the attempts succeeded.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: rubygems, rubydoc-info, jfrog-artifactory

Vendors: openai, ruby-central, jfrog
